assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only three-days-of-happiness:miyagi@original-novel#novel-monograph (the canonical v1.0 Miyagi novel monograph, qualified COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY, accepted with corrections and passed on receiving review against the Japanese EPUB) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the single Japanese witness TDH-JP-01, native chapters 2-15 (she does not appear in chapter 1), end paratext excluded. The readings, the longitudinal notebook, the novel synthesis, the completion audit, the release-decision record and the Kusunoki, Himeno, Shinbashi and substitute-watcher monographs are not cited, and nothing is borrowed from them. The audit's readiness table, its RETROSPECTIVE_CONSISTENCY_TEST caution and the project's statement that no reconstruction operation is authorized were read as method inputs, not conclusions. No translation, adaptation or other edition is assessed, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: From the shop on day 0 (Ch02 P0109-P0185, unnamed clerk) through her return and the plan for three days (Ch15 P0121), with her recounted history from about age six to ten (Ch08 P0069-P0074; Ch11 P0203-P0205) used as her testimony. States are split at the station night (Ch08 P0007-P0091), her disappearance for two days (Ch12 P0004-P0007), the price-lie concession and confession (Ch12 P0138-P0193, with P0193 dividing testimony given before and after her admission of lies), her objection and requests (Ch13 P0016-P0087), the plea and farewell (Ch14 P0110-P0152) and the return (Ch15 P0053-P0108). Day counts are the monograph's approximate inferences. Nothing after Ch15 P0127 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a specialist account of Miyagi, Kusunoki's watcher: stated values (small certain happiness, Ch05 P0025; things that last, Ch11 P0066; being treated as present, Ch12 P0183), fears by testimony, a coping repertoire of irony, the work frame and control of information, and a self-conception of self-deprecation. A conduct-level mechanism is located: she manages the conflict between duty and feeling through information, by a lie that gives, lies that protect and concealment that spares (section 5). Not B: except where conduct shows them, her motives come only from hedged self-interpretation, and at Ch12 P0193 she says many of her statements were lies without naming them all; care and duty remain undecided rivals for the early chapters, the price lie's aim (at him, or at anyone) is undecidable, and the motive for her final sale is unstated. Being unable to tell which motive decides is insufficiency. Not D: a graded testimony table and located mechanisms support narrow extrapolation.

The monograph separates what changes in Miyagi (register, distance, stance toward visibility, outlook, role in the giving; section 14.1) from what is only revealed late (her history, the price lie, the rule lies, her drawing; section 14.2) and what stays constant (politeness to him, self-deprecation, watchfulness, the posture, mirroring his words). Each phase is located (Ch02, Ch03-Ch07, Ch08, Ch09-Ch11, Ch12, Ch13, Ch14, Ch15). Counterevidence: the causes of change are mainly her testimony, and her statements about her future serve different purposes and are not a sequence of forecasts. Not A: that. Not C: located change of conduct and register across contexts, kept apart from revelation.

Miyagi's written Japanese voice is documented by phase: shop keigo and the institutional 我々 (Ch02), business-polite drifting to colloquial-polite with sentence-final から (Ch03-Ch07), the first えっと and ごめんなさい at the station (Ch08), playful polite (Ch09-Ch11), rude content in polite form (Ch12-Ch13), pleading (Ch14) and ただいま (Ch15). Address is exhaustive: only あなた and クスノキさん to him, never あんた; 私; さん for others. Plain main clauses to him are enumerated as three exceptions, plain trailing clauses cluster in emotional disclosure, and apologies are graded from 申し訳ありません to ごめんなさい. Counterevidence: all of it is written register in Kusunoki's record, with no interior voice. Not A: she is never clearly shown angry, and register toward a superior or institution is evidenced only by the shop. Not C: a located, near-exhaustive register and address system across phases.

Miyagi's ordinary conduct on duty is located across many scenes: the corner and hugged knees (Ch03 P0059), five steps behind him (Ch03 P0074), the observation notebook, broken sleep (Ch07 P0090), separate purchases and no alcohol while working (Ch04 P0060-P0075), the daily question about his day, public discretion; with food, whistling, crane-folding, likes and dislikes, and an explicit account of which duty habits change once relations change and which preferences look stable (section 11). Not A: her life off duty, on days off and with other watchers is unknown. Not C: recurring, located habits with a stable-versus-situational account.

Toward Kusunoki the monograph gives a phase-by-phase table of Miyagi's conduct and stated stance from shop to return (section 9.1). Other relations are thin or mediated: her mother and aunt only through her testimony; her childhood friend, Enishi, through her account and one wordless scene whose feelings are not narrated (Ch13 P0139-P0155); the substitute watcher through his testimony; Shinbashi's circle and the Ch15 crowd briefly. Not B: only one relationship is sampled in depth, and why her conduct toward Kusunoki changes rests on her own testimony (Ch12 P0183). Not D: the Kusunoki relation is located phase by phase with directional conduct.

The text never shows Miyagi's interior directly; it reaches the page through her conduct, her testimony and Kusunoki's hedged readings, and the monograph grades her testimony item by item (section 1.3), including her disclosures of history (Ch08), of her friend (Ch11 P0203-P0205), of love (Ch12 P0183-P0189) and of being already saved (Ch13 P0085). Her most unguarded recorded speech is a wish said to a man she thinks is pretending to sleep (Ch11 P0010). Not C: no direct interior access, and statements after Ch12 P0193 cannot rest on her word alone. Not E: the disclosures are substantial, distributed across chapters, and graded.

Miyagi does not escalate (section 6.4): conditional apology and warning (Ch03 P0122-P0124), no insistence when he shakes off her sleeve, sharing his soaking rather than insisting (Ch10 P0210-P0223). Under threat she states a deterrent coldly, does not flee and stiffens (Ch08 P0011-P0039); confronted with her lie she evades and denies four times before conceding through reasons, apology and an offer of punishment (Ch12 P0140-P0197); in grief she refuses, pleads and weeps (Ch14 P0129-P0145). Not B: the threat and the confrontation are single full cases that the profile rates weak to moderate, why she stayed in Ch08 is unknown, and she is never clearly shown angry. Not D: a consistent, located non-escalation pattern.

Miyagi's ethically weighted acts are located: the price lie that gave him her money, the rule lies she calls expedients to protect herself (Ch12 P0193), concealment of Himeno's plan (Ch10 P0169-P0180), non-intervention in his trespass and reading of the capsule letters, objection to his sacrifice (Ch13 P0025), and by her account her own final sale (Ch15 P0090-P0105), with a capacity-versus-willingness list (section 13). Her reasons are hedged testimony, partly from after P0193. Not C: there is no account of how she weighs right against wrong beyond the information mechanism, and the reasons for the decisive acts are unverified or unstated. Not E: the acts are substantial and recur across the novel.

Miyagi's humor is analyzed by form and phase (section 7.3): dry deflation (Ch03 P0114; Ch04 P0081), irony inside polite form (Ch05 P0043-P0045; Ch06 P0109), the needle about Himeno (Ch07 P0039), the first shared joke (Ch08 P0085-P0086), mock-formal handling of compliments that Kusunoki later plays back to her (Ch10 P0038-P0040; Ch12 P0133), teasing (Ch10 P0058; Ch13 P0063), play-boasting (Ch11 P0111) and joining the crowd's fiction on her return (Ch15 P0063, P0079). Not A: her humor reaches the page only through his record. Not C: forms are located and phased, from dry irony to teasing.

The novel is complete, and the monograph covers Miyagi in every chapter in which she appears (Ch02-Ch15), with locators and routes to readings and notebook IDs (section 18), after a fidelity review with more than fifty source checks and a receiving review of the revised portrait against the Japanese EPUB, according to the discovery row. Not A: one derived synthesis whose locators resolve outside the cited set, and reviews the project calls bounded. Not C: whole-work coverage routed to stable IDs.

The evidence affirmatively bounds Miyagi: testimony she retracted or that events contradicted is graded (the floor price, the misconduct and distance rules, "no one will ever again try to like you"); contradictions she leaves standing are listed (section 4); gaps where the text had an opportunity are named (the grave wish never returns, buying back lifespan is never raised, her reaction to his sale and to his drawing is not narrated); and abstention zones are explicit (section 16). Not A: some bounds are unknowns with no opportunity in the text. Not C: located retractions and contradictions, not only silences.

Miyagi's states are located by approximate day (day 0 to about day 58), by register phase with anchors, and by a disclosure-order table of what she told and when (section 3.2), with Ch12 P0193 as a dated division of her testimony. Not A: the days are inferences and the record's revision points are unknown. Not C: an explicit, anchored sequence.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, and only toward Kusunoki: polite main clauses as the strong default under pressure, with only the narrow attested own-voice exceptions (the plain disclosure 「…知りたくなかった。」 at Ch11 P0205 and the plain exclamation 「こういうの、好きだなあ」 at Ch13 P0059); her imitation of Himeno at Ch10 P0062 is role speech, not her register; あなた or クスノキさん, never あんた or his bare name; 私; さん for others.

Register follows the selected phase (shop keigo in Ch02, cool colloquial-polite with sentence-final から in Ch03-Ch07, playful polite from Ch09, rude content in polite form in Ch12-Ch13, pleading in Ch14); plain trailing clauses (〜から, 〜のに, 〜ので) only in emotional disclosure.
No line of anger at him, no register toward a superior or institution beyond the shop, and no interior monologue.
scenario_readiness.note: A located, near-exhaustive register and address system constrains short illustrative lines for Miyagi toward Kusunoki at a selected phase; the absence of an interior voice and of anger keeps the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions are conduct-level and use only the profile's rows (section 16): deflating grand plans early; warning him off past relationships while not stopping a push from his own past; answering questions about the system readily in quasi-legal form; deflecting questions about herself until gently pressed; mock-formal deflection of compliments; trying once to stop self-harm, then sharing his condition; objecting with gratitude to a sacrifice for her and, in extremity, pleading.

Her motives are presented as open where the evidence leaves them open (care or duty early; whom the price lie was for; why she stayed in Ch08; why she sold in Ch15), with her testimony graded, not adopted.
Nothing is generated about the true rules of the system, her real valuation, or her inner response to Enishi.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One selected phase from the shop (Ch02) to the return (Ch15 P0053-P0121): the clerk (Ch02); the early watcher (Ch03-Ch07); the station night (Ch08); the softened companion (Ch09-Ch11); disclosure (Ch12, before or after P0193); objection (Ch13); plea and farewell (Ch14); or the return (Ch15).
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kusunoki, as the watched subject, in the relationship state of the selected phase. Strangers who cannot perceive her only as settings for conduct with him; Shinbashi's circle and the Ch15 crowd only in the brief registers sampled. Her mother, her aunt, Enishi, the substitute watcher and other watchers are excluded as interlocutors.
setting_constraints: The novel's world, with her on duty as a watcher perceivable only by the watched, or, in Ch15, visible to all.
Places and routines of the kinds shown with Kusunoki; no off-duty life, days off or other subjects.

scenario_readiness.note: The operational profile supports narrow, conduct-level extrapolation for Miyagi in sampled situations with Kusunoki at a selected phase. Her motives and the true rules are not established, so novel scenarios stay at the level of observed conduct.

conditions: Duty habits in the early phases (the corner, the notebook, separate meals, no alcohol, broken sleep, public discretion); shared meals, the bed and open affection after relations change.
Public scenes follow her stance of the selected phase: warning him against speaking to her, then delighted acknowledgement and handshakes in Ch14, then wit with strangers when seen in Ch15.
No off-duty life and no extended conduct toward anyone but Kusunoki.
scenario_readiness.note: Located daily routine and public conduct support bounded everyday scenes for Miyagi with Kusunoki.

Miyagi's reasons for her ethically weighted acts are hedged testimony from someone who says she lied about many things (Ch12 P0193), and the motives of the decisive acts are undecided or unstated. Ethical deliberation in a new situation would be invention.

conditions: Toward Kusunoki only, in the selected phase: distance kept on duty; the bed shared back to back and then face to face; embraces after her confession; teasing; refusal to be forgotten and pleading in Ch14.
Her love is her testimony (Ch12 P0183-P0188); it is not presented as verified fact, and her inner response to Enishi is not modeled.
No sexual or intimate preference beyond what the monograph records.
scenario_readiness.note: Miyagi's intimate conduct toward Kusunoki is located by phase; her stated love is testimony that fits her conduct, and her feeling for Enishi is not narrated.

conditions: Shop conduct and keigo as in Ch02; watcher routines (following, the observation notebook, the answer check formula, warnings in public, non-intervention).
Her statements about the rules are testimony; the misconduct and distance rules are her admitted lies, and the true rules, her reporting powers and her valuation are not generated.
No conduct toward superiors, headquarters or other watchers.
scenario_readiness.note: Miyagi's work as clerk and watcher is densely sampled at the level of conduct and register; what the system really requires is not established.

known_limits.statement: Almost every load-bearing fact about Miyagi's past, motives and the system rests on her word. At Ch12 P0193 she says she has told many lies, naming two by way of example; earlier testimony is uncertain item by item and later testimony cannot rest on her word alone.
The novel never shows Miyagi's interior directly; it reaches the page through her conduct, her testimony and Kusunoki's readings of her face and tone, which the monograph keeps hedged.

For Miyagi, care and duty remain undecided rivals for the early chapters; the price lie has three hedged motives and whether it was aimed at Kusunoki or at anyone is undecidable; why she stayed in Ch08 is unknown; and her motive and timing for the final sale are unstated.
Miyagi's conduct at length is shown only toward Kusunoki; her mother, aunt and the substitute watcher reach the page through testimony, and her feelings on seeing Enishi are not narrated.
Miyagi is never clearly shown angry at Kusunoki (her closest moments are sulking and pleading), and her register toward a superior or an institution is evidenced only by the shop scene.
The novel narrates Miyagi's return and the plan for three days and only projects the rest; what she sold is lifespan only by strong inference, and nothing after Ch15 P0127 is established.

Miyagi is seen through Kusunoki's record, most of whose early chapters were first written about day 30, before the price-lie hint and her confession; which passages were revised later is unknown (TDH-C010).
The cited evidence contains no reconstruction model, probe or held-out evaluation of Miyagi; the monograph's operational profile is a literary reading aid it states has not been tested.
